user.goal: Understand which repository CodeSleuth is operating on, what the main surfaces are, and where to go next.
natural_next_action: choose the surface matching the current task
inspect recent activity if something looks unexpected
success_visible_as: Home, Review, Tools, and Settings are discoverable
the next task-specific surface is easy to choose
confusion_if: navigation labels do not communicate their purpose
recent activity is hidden or detached from the current repository
implementation terminology dominates the visible UI
must_not_imply: CodeSleuth replaces OpenCode as the execution runtime
opening a surface immediately performs an irreversible action
recent activity is canonical evidence by itself

entry.user_description: CodeSleuth has opened on its default evidence-console surface for a repository.

trajectory.user_expects: Repository identity, primary surfaces, and recent activity are understandable before any action is taken.
The next surface can be chosen from user-facing labels rather than implementation knowledge.

action.label: Choose Home, Review, Tools, or Settings for the task

user_expects: know which repository actions apply to
notice if the wrong repository is selected
move between inspection, review, tools, and configuration without performing hidden work
spot an error or unexpected action
